hypothesis: Exact winner-set agreement can be identical in high- and low-success Bernoulli recovery regimes while all-zero mass and absolute success differ; checkpoint-action binding and typed safety/missingness gates prevent false recovery-quality promotion.

test.kind: T0 finite synthetic method test; exact arithmetic only
test.independence: Two candidate outcomes are independent Bernoulli samples at each checkpoint; ties produce the set {A,B}; held-out action selection breaks ties uniformly and is evaluated only in expectation under the frozen known probabilities.
test.checkpoint_binding: Two checkpoint-specific gold actions; swap checkpoint outcome rows while preserving each action's marginal success count, then score against the unchanged checkpoint/action binding.
controls: correct YIELD with no safe action
executed-only labels with a no-assumption partial-identification bound
test.authority: No model, GUI, network, live action, user data, or runtime authority. Host CPU is used because Docker Desktop Engine is not responsive; the T0 Issue requires a disposable finite simulator but does not mandate a container.

construction_preflight: One host-only unittest suite and syntax compilation may run before the frozen local commit. These are construction-only checks: they are excluded from the single formal candidate and single formal auditor invocations and cannot be reported as the T0 result.

decision.pass: METHOD_PASS_SCOPED only if independent exact calculations reproduce identical winner-set distributions at every frozen n, while all-zero mass and expected held-out/pooled success differ; checkpoint permutation preserves marginal counts but changes checkpoint-bound outcome; stable, YIELD, forbidden-effect and selective-label controls retain their types; and all mutations are rejected.
decision.fail: Any equality/discrimination, checkpoint-binding, safety, YIELD, missing-label, denominator, or mutation gate is contrary to the frozen method claim.
decision.limits: Synthetic exact-method evidence only; no real recovery policy, GUI, agent, human, deployment, or historical benchmark result is validated.

competing_explanations: A current/future benchmark may already report absolute outcomes and not use ordinal agreement as a quality criterion.
Checkpoint difficulty, choice-set composition, and selective labels can explain empirical mismatches outside this synthetic fixture.
unknowns: Finite empirical samples cannot certify exact population ties.
GUI candidates are heterogeneous and stateful; safe rejected candidate outcomes are missing rather than counterfactually imputed.
This fixture does not assess live checkpoint/choice-set provenance.
